title: Introduce helm gate controller and staged hook ramping for private installs
author: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Private upgrades that introduce new or modified helm hook jobs (migrations, cert sync, preflight probes) often cause cascading retries and noisy alerts when a fleet of tenants all execute the same hook concurrently. We need an operational guard that lets the chart coordinate a staged ramp of hook executions across tenant installs (or across replicas in a single tenant) so upgrades are smoother and safer.

This PR adds a lightweight helm gate controller and values-driven staged hook ramping primitives to the private helm chart. The goal is to provide an opt-in, backwards-compatible mechanism to: 1) schedule hook waves with delay/jitter, 2) elect a single hook leader per-namespace for critical migrations, 3) expose observability for hook progress and throttling, and 4) allow safe rollback by fencing subsequent waves.

Design highlights: values.schema.yaml additions (hookGate.* and hookRamping.*), small templating helpers under templates/_hook-gate.tpl, a new preupgrade job template that consults a ConfigMap-based gate, a leader-election helper annotation for initJobs, and a migration note explaining operator-less mode for air-gapped installs. The implementation favors not introducing a new long-lived controller binary by implementing a minimal gate that leverages Kubernetes primitives (ConfigMap + preupgrade job semantics) and documented operational commands for On-Prem teams.

Migration/upgrade plan: default values keep existing behaviour (gate disabled). To opt-in, operators set values.hookGate.enabled=true and configure waves. A short migration job is included to populate initial gate state when enabling ramping on clusters with existing releases. Rollback path: gates can be closed (set enabled=false) which causes remaining waves to be skipped; the preupgrade job has a fence-check that marks the release as unsafe to proceed when rollbacks are required.

Rationale: we've had two incidents where simultaneous init-migrations overwhelmed DB proxies during a tenant upgrade window. Staggering and leader election at the chart level reduces blast radius for customers who deploy using Helm-based automation (private installer + on-prem).

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative — no new controllers are added to the runtime image. Future follow-ups may extract the gate into a small daemon for cross-namespace coordination if the ConfigMap pattern proves limiting.
review_comments: Luca Hernandez: Nice approach to avoid adding operators. Two questions: 1) can the ConfigMap gating scale to 500 namespaces? 2) Can we make the default wave wait configurable by seconds rather than minutes?

Maya Patel: Answered — the gate uses per-namespace keys and is sharded by release name; worst-case we add a lightweight daemon in a follow-up. Wave timing is now seconds-granular in values.schema and validated in chart tests.
Priya Rao: Please add a metric-emitting annotation or label so observability can correlate which wave is in progress. Also requested adding an e2e that simulates two concurrent upgrades.
Maya Patel: Added wave.label and included a small prometheus-style metric annotation in NOTES and test harness. E2E is tracked in ENG-3347 follow-up (will require test infra changes).
Omar Bennett: Confirmed no new RBAC scopes are introduced other than read/write to ConfigMaps in the release namespace. Approving after a minor nitfix on templating helper names.
Maya Patel: Fixed helper names and rebased onto main after the release branch reformat changes.

merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2024-11-02 via web UI. The squash commit includes values.schema changes, helper templates, preupgrade/migrate seeding job, tests, and docs. Release notes updated to mention the opt-in nature and example values. No post-merge migrations required beyond enabling the gate in values for tenants who want ramping.
release_notes: Added opt-in 'hookGate' and 'hookRamping' values to the redwood-private chart to enable staged execution of helm hooks (preupgrade/init jobs). Default is disabled; enables safer rolling of migration hooks and provides leader-election helpers and observability labels. See docs/private/upgrade-guides/staged-hook-ramping.md for examples and migration steps.
